correctness.rationale: Starting from Theorem 4.6 of arXiv:2210.00816, membership is exactly q>=beta(r). Isolation is equivalent to q=beta(r)-1 plus strict local maximum of beta(r), with terminal residue separately handled. Left ascent iff Fibonacci digit 2 is selected; right descent iff digit 4 is also selected (using 2F_2+F_4=F_5 and summand minimality). Every independent subset of indices 6,...,a-1 yields exactly one gap, so the Fibonacci and binomial formulas follow. Direct DP and Dijkstra checks matched all gaps for a=3,...,22 (435045 exact membership decisions). Finite checks supplement, not substitute, the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact Apéry data is a stronger *membership description*, so every individual gap is computable from prior work. The proposed contribution is not a new membership oracle: it is the independent closed classification of neighbor-isolated gaps, their Fibonacci number and binomial grading. Pseudo-Frobenius elements test addition by every positive semigroup element, whereas isolation tests the integers immediately adjacent to the gap. These subsets are not equivalent and the 2025 theorem does not state the isolated-gap count. The 2023 perfect-semigroup paper provides general algorithms rather than this symbolic Fibonacci family result.

value.rationale: Isolated gaps are the local obstruction to perfectness, distinct from Frobenius number, genus and pseudo-Frobenius type. An entire natural infinite Fibonacci-shifted semigroup family receives a complete exact isolation classification, cardinality F_(a-4), grading by gap level and sharp parity-split largest isolated gap. These are structurally motivated, not arbitrary finite cases; the known Apéry data alone does not state this closed enumeration.
